title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Zscaler
providers.scope_notes: Covers Zscaler (ZIA, ZPA, OneAPI via Authentication Service / ZIdentity). SaaS; OneAPI needs services linked to Authentication Service; legacy ZIA API needs an API subscription; Workflow Automation, Client Connector and ZDX API keys not covered.

controls.name: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server status / delete
controls.what: Disable or delete a trusted external authorization server.
controls.setting: Administration > API > Internet & SaaS API > OAuth 2.0 Authorization Servers

controls.name: Required JWT claims (audience, issuer, client ID)
controls.what: Mandate claim checks on external tokens.

controls.name: API Roles
controls.what: Per-category Full/View Only/None permissions; cannot modify admins.
controls.setting: Administration > Role Management > Internet & SaaS > Add API Role

controls_unknown: Source-IP restriction for OneAPI clients, ZPA keys or legacy ZIA sessions (Admin Sign-On Policy and ZIA restricted admin access pages do not state API coverage)
Whether the Authentication Service Admin Sign-On Policy or MFA applies to legacy ZIA API password logins
Whether deleting/disabling a ZPA API key or ZIA authorization server ends already-issued bearer tokens
Whether API client create/delete and token revoke appear as named actions in Authentication Service audit logs (documented actions are generic Create/Update/Delete)
Whether read-only (GET) API calls are recorded in any audit log
Expiry of JWT key pairs (zscaler-2) and Sandbox tokens
OneAPI rate limits (only legacy limits fetched)

auth_paths.name: ZIA OAuth 2.0 with external authorization server (PingFederate, Okta, Entra ID)

authentication.summary: A client app registered in the customer's IdP gets a client-credentials JWT with scope <cloud>::<orgid>::<API role>; ZIA validates the signature via the server's JWKS and the scope claim.

federation.details: ZIA trusts tokens issued by the customer's PingFederate, Okta or Entra ID; audience, issuer and client ID claims can be required.

ip_restriction.boundary: Not documented on the ZIA side; any IP policy would be the external IdP's.

lifetime.summary: Token lifetime set in the external OAuth service

renewal.summary: Client requests a new token from its IdP.

administration.summary: Admins add, edit, enable/disable or delete authorization servers; API roles (up to 16, rank 7, cannot modify admins) set what the client can do.
administration.conditions: Requires API subscription and API roles; cloud service API only.

offboard.details: Client-credentials grant works outside the context of users.

inventory.details: Zscaler lists configured authorization servers; the individual OAuth clients live in the external IdP.

inventory.ui: ZIA Admin Portal > Administration > Cloud Service API Security > OAuth 2.0 Authorization Servers tab (servers only; list OAuth clients in the external IdP)

expiry.ui: Set in the external OAuth service, e.g. Okta: authorization server > Access Policies > rule > Access token lifetime is. Check expires_in in the token response

token_format.notes: JWT issued by the customer's IdP.

log_sources.name: ZIA audit logs
log_sources.notes: Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Internet & SaaS; records Admin UI and API actions; 6-month retention; NSS admin audit feed.

anomaly_cues: API changes by oauth-<role> user from unknown IPs

containment.steps: Disable or delete the authorization server in ZIA; disable the client in the IdP; tighten the API role.
containment.notes: Docs do not say whether ZIA rejects already-issued, unexpired JWTs after IdP-side revocation.

unknown: Effect of disabling the server on live tokens
Which IdP client made a call (only role user is logged)

calls.log_notes: Audit logs record actions; GETs not confirmed

calls.reveals: URL categories (up to 100 URLs per request)
